Regression GPBoost Learner

Source: R/learner_gpboost_regr_gpboost.R
mlr_learners_regr.gpboost.Rd

Tree-boosting combined with Gaussian process and grouped random effects models. Calls gpboost::gpb.train() from gpboost.

The random effects model is specified with the custom parameters group_data_cols and gp_coords_cols. If neither is set, a plain gradient boosting model is fitted. The boosting parameters are documented here and in the documentation of gpboost::gpb.train(). The parameters of the random effects model are documented in gpboost::GPModel().

Custom mlr3 parameters

  • group_data_cols: Names of features that define grouped random effects, one random intercept per column. The columns are passed to gpboost::GPModel() as group_data and are excluded from the tree features.

  • gp_coords_cols: Names of numeric features that are the coordinates of a Gaussian process. The columns are passed to gpboost::GPModel() as gp_coords and are excluded from the tree features.

  • seed is passed to the boosting algorithm and to gpboost::GPModel().

  • nrounds sets the number of boosting iterations. The alias num_iterations is not available.

  • Observation weights are passed to gpboost::GPModel() if a random effects model is used and to gpboost::gpb.Dataset() otherwise.

  • The predict type "se" returns the square root of the predictive variance and requires a random effects model.

Initial parameter values

  • num_threads is initialized to 1 to avoid conflicts with parallelization via future.

  • verbose is initialized to -1 to suppress the output of GPBoost.

Dictionary

This Learner can be instantiated via lrn():

lrn("regr.gpboost")

Meta Information

  • Task type: “regr”

  • Predict Types: “response”, “se”

  • Feature Types: “logical”, “integer”, “numeric”, “factor”, “ordered”

Usage

LearnerRegrGPBoost$new()

LearnerRegrGPBoost$importance()

The importance scores are extracted with gpboost::gpb.importance() and correspond to the total gain of the splits of a feature. Features without splits and the columns of the random effects model get an importance of 0.

Usage

Examples

# Define the Learner with a random intercept for the number of cylinders
learner = lrn("regr.gpboost", group_data_cols = "cyl", min_data_in_leaf = 5L, predict_type = "se")
print(learner)
#> 
#> ── <LearnerRegrGPBoost> (regr.gpboost): Gaussian Process Boosting ──────────────
#> • Model: -
#> • Parameters: group_data_cols=cyl, verbose=-1, num_threads=1,
#> min_data_in_leaf=5
#> • Packages: mlr3, mlr3extralearners, and gpboost
#> • Predict Types: response and [se]
#> • Feature Types: logical, integer, numeric, factor, and ordered
#> • Encapsulation: none (fallback: -)
#> • Properties: importance, marshal, missings, and weights
#> • Other settings: use_weights = 'use', predict_raw = 'FALSE'

# Define a Task
task = tsk("mtcars")

# Create train and test set
ids = partition(task)

# Train the learner on the training ids
learner$train(task, row_ids = ids$train)
#> [GPBoost] [Info] GPBoost is using 1 OpenMP thread by default for parallel computations. Run gpb.tune.num.threads() to benchmark different numbers of threads and to select a tuned default for this session. For the best performance, try different values of 'num_parallel_threads' on the 'GPModel' you are using.

print(learner$importance())
#>       qsec         am       disp       carb       drat        cyl       gear 
#> 0.32248478 0.27737308 0.19200672 0.16217568 0.04595974 0.00000000 0.00000000 
#>         hp         vs         wt 
#> 0.00000000 0.00000000 0.00000000 

# Make predictions for the test rows
predictions = learner$predict(task, row_ids = ids$test)

# Score the predictions
predictions$score()
#> regr.mse 
#> 10.29927
